title: Learned prepositions and frozen datives: εν τω μεταξύ, εκ των υστέρων, άνευ όρων
goal: Own the hundred or so fixed learned phrases that every educated Greek uses, and the prepositions behind them.

blocks.text: The dative case died in spoken Greek a thousand years ago, and so did prepositions like εν, εκ, προ, υπέρ, άνευ. But they survive in **fixed phrases** that are not learned or bookish at all: *εν τω μεταξύ* is as normal as 'meanwhile', *τοις μετρητοίς* is what the shopkeeper asks. Treat each phrase as a single word; don't try to build new ones. The case after the old preposition is usually the genitive (where the ancient language had the genitive) and the frozen datives keep their **-ω, -η, -οις, -αις** endings.

blocks.text:
**Two traps.** *Εν τάξει* vs *εντάξει*: the first means 'in order' (*Όλα εν τάξει με τα χαρτιά σας*), the second is the everyday 'OK'; both spellings are correct for 'OK'. *Κατά* + genitive means 'against' (*κατά της απόφασης*), + accusative 'during, according to, about' (*κατά τη γνώμη μου, κατά τις δέκα*).

**υπό την προϋπόθεση ότι/να** 'provided that' and **εκ των υστέρων** 'in hindsight' are the two phrases from this list that will most quickly raise your spoken register.

blocks.title: Ο εν λόγω κύριος
blocks.text: Greeks use learned phrases with a wink as often as seriously. *Ο εν λόγω κύριος* 'the gentleman in question' is how you refer, slightly ironically, to someone everyone is gossiping about. *Εν ψυχρώ* 'in cold blood' is a newspaper staple for crimes. And when a waiter in a village says *Τοις μετρητοίς, παρακαλώ*, he isn't being formal; it's simply the set phrase for 'cash only'.

blocks.title: Μια συνέντευξη εξ αποστάσεως
blocks.en:
— Professor, in short, what is the conclusion of your research?

— At first sight the results are encouraging. Children who attended lessons remotely during the pandemic did not, on average, fall far behind. However, the picture changes when we examine the data in depth: the gap to the detriment of poorer families was unprecedented.

— So, in hindsight, closing the schools was a mistake?

— I'm not saying that. In any case, the decision was taken without knowledge of much of the data. What I propose is that we return to in-person teaching, provided that the digital tools are kept, and invest in lifelong learning for teachers.

— And for the time being?

— For the time being we need time. We'll see the conclusions in due course.
